questions.question:
D1 — Add gstack skill routing rules to CLAUDE.md?
Project/branch/task: gstack-plan-count-FDFfod on main, reviewing PLAN.md (saved project views).
ELI10: gstack skills work best when the project's CLAUDE.md tells the agent which skill to reach for (bugs → /investigate, scope → /plan-ceo-review, etc.). Without it you invoke skills by hand each time. Stakes are low either way. Note: plan mode is active, so if you say yes the CLAUDE.md edit and commit happen after this review exits plan mode.
Stakes if we pick wrong: mild friction only; reversible with one config command.
Recommendation: A because routing rules make future sessions pick the right skill without you remembering names.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Add routing rules (recommended)
  ✅ Future sessions auto-route bugs, scope, ship, and QA requests to the right skill
  ✅ One-time, committed to the repo so teammates get it too
  ❌ Adds ~20 lines to CLAUDE.md; must wait until plan mode exits to write it
B) No thanks
  ✅ Keeps CLAUDE.md exactly as the fixture defines it right now
  ✅ Nothing written, nothing committed; re-enable any time via gstack-config
  ❌ You invoke every skill manually going forward
Net: convenience later vs an untouched CLAUDE.md now.

options.label: Add routing rules (recommended)
options.description: Append the skill routing section to CLAUDE.md and commit once plan mode exits.

questions.question:
D2 — Enable cross-project learnings search?
Project/branch/task: same repo, same review.
ELI10: gstack records small lessons per project (command quirks, pitfalls). It can also search lessons from your other projects on this machine to spot patterns that apply here. Everything stays local; no data leaves the machine. Good for solo devs; skip if you juggle multiple client codebases where cross-talk would be awkward.
Stakes if we pick wrong: reversible with one config command; worst case a slightly less informed review.
Recommendation: A because this is a solo fixture repo and more prior context only helps.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Enable cross-project learnings (recommended)
  ✅ Reviews get prior lessons from any project on this machine, not just this one
  ✅ Stays fully local; a single config flag you can flip back any time
  ❌ Lessons from unrelated codebases may occasionally surface as noise
B) Keep learnings project-scoped
  ✅ Zero chance of one client's patterns leaking into another's review
  ✅ Simpler mental model: what you see came from this repo only
  ❌ This repo has zero learnings today, so the review starts cold
Net: broader context vs strict per-project isolation.

options.label: Enable cross-project (recommended)
options.description: Search learnings across all local projects.

options.label: Project-scoped only
options.description: Only this repo's learnings are used.

questions.question:
D3 — Run /office-hours first, or proceed with the standard review?
Project/branch/task: same repo; no design doc exists for this branch.
ELI10: /office-hours produces a structured problem statement, a premise challenge, and explored alternatives for this specific feature. It gives the CEO review sharper input, at the cost of roughly ten more minutes of Q&A. The plan here is short (4 approach bullets), so the review can run without it, but the premise challenge will be based on what I infer rather than what you told me.
Stakes if we pick wrong: a review built on a misread premise, or ten minutes spent restating what you already know.
Recommendation: B because the plan's goal is concrete and well-bounded; the review's Step 0 already runs a premise challenge, and I can offer office-hours mid-review if the premise turns out to be shaky.
Note: options differ in kind, not coverage — no completeness score.
A) Run /office-hours now
  ✅ Produces a written design doc that later reviews and teammates can read
  ✅ Explores alternatives to saved views before we commit to reviewing this shape
  ❌ About ten minutes of additional questions before the review starts (human ~10 min / CC ~10 min)
B) Skip, standard review (recommended)
  ✅ Starts the review immediately on the plan as written
  ✅ Step 0 still challenges the premise and proposes implementation alternatives
  ❌ No persisted design doc; premise reasoning rests on my inference from the plan text
Net: sharper input later vs starting now on a plan that is already fairly clear.

options.label: Run /office-hours now
options.description: Build a design doc first, then resume the review.

options.label: Skip, standard review (recommended)
options.description: Proceed directly to Step 0 of the CEO review.
